Questions and answers

Questions and answers

What is Carte de Pression au Sol?

In this glossary, Carte de Pression au Sol refers to: Synoptic weather map depicting isobars and pressure systems at mean sea level, used for routeing decisions.

How is Carte de Pression au Sol used in maritime?

In maritime communication, this term appears in contexts such as: "Navigateur, mettez à jour le plan de voyage à l’aide de la carte de pression au sol 0000 UTC indiquant une dépression en creusement au sud-ouest de l’Islande et un passage frontal prévu."

Why does Carte de Pression au Sol matter in maritime?

Carte de Pression au Sol matters because it supports clear communication in Meteorology contexts for Deck Officers, Engine Officers, and Masters. It also connects to aviation training and exam language such as STCW, Marlins Test, ISF Watchkeeper, and GMDSS.

Who uses Carte de Pression au Sol?

Carte de Pression au Sol is mainly used by Deck Officers, Engine Officers, and Masters.

Where does this definition come from?

This definition is sourced from IMO SMCP, STCW Convention, SOLAS, COLREG and published by Protermify Maritime as a static maritime reference page.

Definition

Synoptic weather map depicting isobars and pressure systems at mean sea level, used for routeing decisions.

Operational example

Navigator, update voyage plan using latest 0000 UTC surface pressure chart showing deepening low south-west of Iceland and forecast frontal passage.

Localized term

Carte de Pression au Sol

Localized example

Navigateur, mettez à jour le plan de voyage à l’aide de la carte de pression au sol 0000 UTC indiquant une dépression en creusement au sud-ouest de l’Islande et un passage frontal prévu.
